solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starts with first of three hags

indicators.note: the first of the word three means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: hags are witches in folklore

explanation.surface: A tale of three old crones beginning something together.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts as a verb means jerks or flinches suddenly, which is what a nervous muscle does.

clue.text: Shock generated by musical

explanation.surface: Someone stunned by something they saw on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick mass of head growth, and the famous rock musical of 1967 bears this name.

clue.text: Bohemian tart after joint

indicators.note: after places the pastry word behind the body-part word

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: An arty type eating a pastry after smoking a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as cannabis, fitting the bohemian picture, but it is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemian describes an unconventional, free-living person, much like a flower-child of the sixties.

clue.text: Defence of Queen's assistant for the audience

indicators.note: something said for listeners signals that the spoken sound of a phrase is meant

parts.note: a royal helper might be called a palace aide

explanation.surface: A royal helper serving as protection for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of stakes built as a fortification is a classic defensive barrier.

clue.text: Tie cargoes roughly and put into boxes

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are put together in a loose, disordered way

explanation.surface: Instructions for packing freight by tying it up and boxing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into boxes figuratively is to classify or sort them into groups.

clue.text: Fuse in centre containing high explosive

indicators.note: containing means the word for centre holds the explosive abbreviation inside

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A fuse set in the middle of a bomb packed with explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuse' suggests a detonator, fitting the bomb picture, but here it is a verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse is to join together into one, which is to stick together as a whole.

clue.text: Beginning to spout tiresome bad language

indicators.note: the beginning of the word spout gives only its opening letter

parts.note: something tiresome is wearing

explanation.surface: Someone starting to spew dull, foul-mouthed talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing and use of oaths is what bad language consists of.

clue.text: Growth occurring in thyroid, rarely enlarged initially

definitions.text: Growth occurring in thyroid, rarely enlarged initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A medical note about a swelling in the neck gland.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck is the medical condition described.

clue.text: Endless surprise regarding aggressive woman

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for surprise is cut off

parts.note: to surprise is to amaze
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A shock concerning a combative woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were warrior women, so the name describes a fierce, strong woman.

clue.text: Jailhouse Rock?

explanation.surface: A reference to the famous Elvis Presley song.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, and to stir is also to move or agitate, as rocking does.

clue.text: Nosed around wretched dog's tail? It could be rich!

indicators.note: around means the word for nosed is placed about the other pieces

parts.note: to nose is to pry, so nosed is pried
wretched means vile

indicators.note: the tail of the word dog is its last letter

explanation.surface: A nosy look at a miserable dog's rear end, with a joke about richness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rich gives a person wealth and advantages, so they are well off and advantaged.

clue.text: Select frozen sweet, not cold

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: a choc ice is a chocolate-coated ice-cream bar, a common British treat
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Picking an ice-cream treat that is somehow not cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means of top quality, specially picked out, as fine goods are.

clue.text: Sublime one with short skirt raised on counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
I is the Roman numeral for one
a counter is a table, as in a shop

explanation.surface: Someone in a miniskirt standing up on a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is so excellent that it is beyond copying or matching.

clue.text: Sensible boy facing English in study

indicators.note: in means the boy and English pieces sit inside the word for study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A level-headed lad facing an English lesson in his study.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible thinking is logical and well thought through.

clue.text: Dodgy start taking Independent newspaper

indicators.note: taking means the word for start holds the other pieces

parts.note: to shy is to start, as a frightened horse does
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A suspicious launch involving the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent newspaper' reads as one paper, but splits into I and FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy means untrustworthy and evasive, the look of someone with something to hide.

clue.text: Meticulous even if handling gold

indicators.note: handling means the word for even if holds the gold piece in its hands

parts.note: though means even if
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Being careful even when touching precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meticulous work is complete and careful in every detail.

clue.text: Lie about in stench producing gas

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit inside the word for stench

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: about means the letters of lie are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Lying about a bad smell that comes from a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The light, inert element used in balloons is a noble gas.

clue.text: The majority of river round island's water

indicators.note: round means the word for majority goes around the island piece

parts.note: the most is the majority
I is the abbreviation for island; the 's is just a link
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Most of a river flowing around an island's water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Water in small amounts, such as dampness or condensation, is wetness in the air or on a surface.

clue.text: Wish for a master to take power

indicators.note: to take means the word for master holds the power letter

parts.note: sire is an old word for lord or master

explanation.surface: An ambition for a ruler to seize power.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have an ambition or hope for something.

clue.text: Guides from peak in Andes, oddly

indicators.note: in means the cap-peak word goes inside the odd letters
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of Andes

parts.note: the peak of a cap is its visor

explanation.surface: Mountain guides working from a summit in the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak' suggests a mountain, fitting the Andes, but it is the brim of a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Guides are counsellors who give direction and advice.

clue.text: Parade not exactly holding show

indicators.note: holding means the answer is held within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A procession that is inexact but contains a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: To show is to indicate or signify, as a symbol stands for its meaning.

clue.text: Tired out by Conservative's reputation?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: out means the letters of tired are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's good name worn out through exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is standing or good name, as in a person being a credit to their family.

clue.text: Put inside or execute?

explanation.surface: A question of whether to imprison or kill a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit someone is to send them to prison, and to commit a deed is to carry it out.

clue.text: Crude sign to a man provoking conflict

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are roughly reshaped

explanation.surface: A rude gesture made at a man starting a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is hostility or opposition, the state of being in conflict.

clue.text: Instrument's no lead instrument

indicators.note: no lead means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a flute is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: An instrument without a leading part to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked string instrument with a rounded back, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Young woman's large bottom

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
ass is slang for bottom

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a girl's big behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl.

clue.text: Camp male hugging nearly everybody

indicators.note: hugging means the male word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: An effeminate man embracing almost everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' suggests flamboyant, matching the male, but it is a noun: a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in World War Two.

clue.text: Herald changing year embracing girl

indicators.note: embracing means the reworked letters wrap around the girl word
changing means the letters of year are put in a new order

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A messenger whose year changes as he embraces a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' could be a verb, but it is the noun: a messenger. 'changing' gives EARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald is a messenger or envoy sent on behalf of another.
